subject: Request: KV cache & KMS subprocessor dependency map + evidence
messages:
From: Natalie O'Connor <natalie.oconnor@novamedhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Third-party evidence request: KV cache / KMS dependencies (SOC2/CAIQ/SIG)

Hi Jonas,

Novamed's InfoSec team is doing a narrowed SIG/CAIQ review for our upcoming pilot. Two items we need documented and evidence for:

1) A prioritized list of subprocessors that interact with runtime KV caching (including any vendor that handles cached tokens/keys, telemetry related to cache hits, or metrics collection tied to inference).
2) A diagram and short attestation of the KMS/keyflow used for ephemeral inference keys (who has key access, whether keys are persistent, HSM/KMS provider details, and log retention).

Specifically we need: a CSV roster (vendor, purpose, data categories, access level), the dependency map (PDF), and any SOC 2 / SIG references for Cache vendors. If you have a CAIQ mapping for these components, that would accelerate our intake.

Can you confirm whether Redwood uses any third-party caching services (managed or SaaS) for inference KV caches, and if so — which vendors and what level of access they hold?

Thanks,
Natalie O'Connor
Senior Security Manager, Novamed Health
[email: natalie.oconnor@novamedhealth.com]

--
Please send materials as a single ZIP when possible; we have a controlled intake process.

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Natalie O'Connor <natalie.oconnor@novamedhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Third-party evidence request: KV cache / KMS dependencies (SOC2/CAIQ/SIG)

Hi Natalie — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura (Legal) and Marissa (Trust/Security) — we'll assemble the deliverables.

Quick answers up front:
- Redwood operates an internal in-memory KV cache inside our serving runtime; we do not route customer runtime KV to third-party caching SaaS for production inference.
- We do use two third parties that touch metadata/telemetry for caching behavior: CacheStream (metrics/observability) and TelemetryFlow (aggregated usage telemetry). Neither has access to plaintext model context or customer prompt content; they receive anonymized/hashed cache-key fingerprints and aggregated counters.
- Ephemeral keys for node-to-node secure RPC are minted by our KMS integration (AWS KMS for hosted deployments; customers on Dedicated/Private may use their own KMS).

Marissa — can you confirm log retention and whether we have an attestation for CacheStream's SOC/SIG posture? Laura — tagging you for any contractual redlines if CacheStream needs an NDA amendment for detailed logs.

I will coordinate a single ZIP with: CSV roster, dependency map, KMS flow diagram, and a short narrative mapping to SIG/CAIQ controls. ETA this afternoon.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Third-party evidence request: KV cache / KMS dependencies (SOC2/CAIQ/SIG)

Jonas / Laura — quick clarifying items before we compile:

- Data scope: Natalie said "cached tokens/keys, telemetry related to cache hits" — confirm whether that includes anonymized prompt fingerprints vs any hashed user identifiers. We need to ensure we redact pseudo-identifiers.
- KMS: which customers are on AWS KMS vs customer-managed KMS (I can provide per-account guidance). For hosted customers like Novamed, we use AWS KMS key aliases in a restricted key policy (no human access) and envelope encryption; ephemeral node keys are rotated hourly.
- Evidence formats: Natalie requested CSV + PDF + CAIQ mapping: I'll create a short mapping doc referencing SIG control IDs we satisfy (P9, P12 equivalents) — do we want to attach redacted cache access logs for the prior 90 days or just the retention policy + sample log lines? The customer intake often accepts policy + sample.

Action plan:
- I'll produce: redwood_subprocessor_matrix_v3.xlsx (master roster), kvcache_vendor_roster.csv, ephemeral-kms-flow-diagram.pdf, and a 1-page narrative mapping SIG/CAIQ answers.
- Ben, can you pull a sanitized sample of cache telemetry (hashed keys, timestamps, event types) for inclusion? Make sure no prompt content or PII is present.

Marissa Cole
Head of Trust & Security
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Natalie O'Connor <natalie.oconnor@novamedhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Third-party evidence request: KV cache / KMS dependencies (SOC2/CAIQ/SIG)

Hi Natalie — attaching the requested materials as a single ZIP per your intake guidance. Summary of enclosed items below. If you'd like these split into separate uploads to your portal, tell me and we can post them to the HubSpot intake ticket.

Attachments (in evidence_pack_novamed_20270503.zip):
- redwood_subprocessor_matrix_v3.xlsx — master roster with vendor role, data categories, access level, contractual control references.
- kvcache_vendor_roster.csv — CSV filter focused on caching/telemetry vendors (CacheStream, TelemetryFlow).
- ephemeral-kms-flow-diagram.pdf — diagram showing envelope encryption, hourly ephemeral node keys, and AWS KMS usage.
- sample-cache-telemetry-90d.txt — sanitized sample lines (hashed keys only).
- sig_caiq_mapping.pdf — 2-page mapping referencing SIG questions we answer for caching/KMS components.

Key notes:
- Production KV cache is internal to our runtime; we do not persist cached prompt text to third-party caches. CacheStream and TelemetryFlow only receive hashed cache-key fingerprints and aggregated metrics.
- For Redwood-hosted customers (like Novamed), disk-at-rest encryption + AWS KMS envelope encryption is used; node ephemeral keys are rotated hourly and destroyed after session termination. Dedicated/Private customers can bring their own KMS (BYOK).
- CacheStream has provided a SOC 2 Type II bridge letter and their SIG self-assessment (included in the ZIP). TelemetryFlow is SOC 2 audited for its telemetry pipeline as well — references are in the roster.

If you need:
- per-account KMS alias names we used for Novamed (I can provide those under NDA), or
- a longer retention export (we provided a 90-day sample), let me know.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: evidence_pack_novamed_20270503.zip (contains 6 files)

From: Natalie O'Connor <natalie.oconnor@novamedhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: InfoSec Intake <security-intake@novamedhealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Third-party evidence request: KV cache / KMS dependencies (SOC2/CAIQ/SIG)

Jonas — received, thank you. We'll ingest the ZIP into our vendor portal and loop back with any follow-ups. A couple of quick asks while we validate: please confirm the exact retention period for the sample telemetry (you mentioned 90 days) and whether the attestation for CacheStream applies to the specific cluster region (us-west-2) that Novamed will use.

If everything looks good, we'll schedule a short call with Marissa to go over the SIG mappings next week.

Warmly,
Natalie
Senior Security Manager, Novamed Health
[natalie.oconnor@novamedhealth.com]
